title: GC-201 Buffer pH Adjustment — Ambiguous SOP Step Treated as Operator Slip

grill_input.description_what_happened: Buffer pH measured at 6.87 instead of target 6.95 ± 0.05. Operator recorded measurement but did not re-adjust. Batch released with out-of-spec pH.
grill_input.description_what_should_have_happened: pH should be adjusted to 6.95 ± 0.05 before release. If out of spec, corrective action required.
grill_input.document_deviated_from: SOP-FORM-0412 Rev 3, Section 4.2.1: 'Measure pH using calibrated probe. If reading is outside target range, adjust with 1 M HCl or 1 M NaOH dropwise until in-spec, then re-measure and confirm.'
grill_input.immediate_corrections: Batch GC201-LOT-2024-0156 quarantined. pH re-measured at 6.88 (still OOS). Batch disposition: scrap.
investigation_steps: Operator interview: stated 'I measured 6.87 and thought it was close enough to 6.95, so I did not adjust.'
pH probe calibration check: in-spec (last calibrated 2024-02-12).
No other lots reviewed for similar pH readings.
grill_input.root_cause_description: Operator judgment error. Operator did not follow SOP requirement to adjust pH to within specification range. Operator stated they interpreted 'close enough' as acceptable.
grill_input.impact_assessment: Single batch affected. No released product impacted. Potency and stability data indicate pH 6.87–6.88 is within acceptable range for GC-201 (historical data 6.80–7.10). No patient safety risk identified.

capa.description: Retraining of Operator ID EMP-4521 on SOP-FORM-0412 Section 4.2.1. Emphasis on strict adherence to specification limits and requirement to adjust and re-measure if out of spec.

statements.quote: The SOP says 'adjust with dropwise until in-spec' but it doesn't say what to do if you're only 0.08 pH units away. I thought I could use judgment.
The SOP is clear: 6.95 ± 0.05 is the target. 6.87 is out of spec. The operator should have adjusted. This is a one-off slip.

case_packet.sop_text_full: SOP-FORM-0412 Rev 3, Section 4.2.1 reads: 'Measure pH using calibrated probe. If reading is outside target range [6.95 ± 0.05], adjust with 1 M HCl or 1 M NaOH dropwise until in-spec, then re-measure and confirm.' However, Section 3.1 (Acceptance Criteria) states: 'Buffer pH shall be 6.90–7.00 for release.' These two ranges are contradictory: Section 4.2.1 specifies 6.95 ± 0.05 (6.90–7.00), but the phrase 'until in-spec' is ambiguous—does it mean 6.95 ± 0.05 or the broader 6.90–7.00 range in Section 3.1?
case_packet.operator_interpretation_survey: Post-investigation, Quality conducted informal survey of 8 other operators who perform this step. Results: 3 operators interpreted 'in-spec' as 6.95 ± 0.05 (strict); 4 operators interpreted it as 6.90–7.00 (loose); 1 operator was unsure. No formal documentation of this survey exists.
case_packet.historical_batch_data: Review of last 12 months of GC-201 batches (n=24) shows: 6 batches released with pH 6.88–6.93 (below 6.95 but within 6.90–7.00); all 6 passed stability and potency testing. No adverse trends.
case_packet.probe_calibration_history: FORM-pH-PROBE-04 calibration records show: last calibration 2024-02-12 (in-spec); previous calibration 2024-01-15 (in-spec). No drift noted.
case_packet.procedure_change_history: SOP-FORM-0412 Rev 3 issued 2023-11-01. Rev 2 (prior) stated: 'Adjust pH to 6.95 ± 0.05 or to 6.90–7.00 if 6.95 ± 0.05 cannot be achieved.' Rev 3 removed the fallback language but did not clarify the acceptance range in Section 4.2.1. No change control or training record for Rev 3 transition.
case_packet.operator_emp_4521_history: Operator has 4 years experience, no prior deviations, passed annual SOP training in 2023. Training records do not show specific emphasis on pH adjustment procedure.
case_packet.quality_manager_investigation_notes: Investigator assumed operator error without reviewing SOP internal consistency or other operator interpretations. Investigation closed in 5 days. No cross-functional review with R&D or formulation team.
case_packet.true_root_cause: Procedure ambiguity: SOP-FORM-0412 Rev 3 contains conflicting acceptance ranges (6.95 ± 0.05 vs. 6.90–7.00) and does not clarify which range applies during adjustment. Multiple operators have interpreted the step differently. The SOP change from Rev 2 to Rev 3 removed clarifying language without updating training or conducting a readiness assessment.
